Unerupted and abnormal teeth, maxillary hypoplasia and severe genu valgum define the syndrome; rotated ears do not establish ear dysfunction.
Benign tumour arising in the tongue, an oral gastrointestinal structure.
Latent treponemal infection; active skin or bone damage is not established in the latent stage.
Adenocarcinoma arising in salivary glands, usually minor glands of the palate.
Inherited renal histidine transport defect; intellectual disability, cortical atrophy and sensorineural deafness occur in 80-99%; skeletal and nail abnormalities omitted by cap.
Inherited retinal degeneration with visual field constriction, night blindness and reduced acuity; no extraocular disease established.
Combined immunodeficiency with impaired lymphocyte and antibody function; recurrent infections do not establish intrinsic damage to additional organs.
Chronic sterile inflammatory osteitis causes joint sclerosis, hyperostosis and soft tissue ossification; associated pustulosis is not established as common.
Hereditary immunodeficiency with abnormal lymphoproliferation; hepatitis, lymphoma and other complications do not justify additional organ labels across the umbrella.
Abnormal immune blood-cell proliferation or excess immunoglobulin production; this broad definition does not establish lymphoma, immunodeficiency or autoimmunity throughout.
Squamous carcinoma arising in extrahepatic bile ducts, which belong to the hepatic axis.
Neoplasm occupying the hypothalamus; endocrine dysfunction is not established as common across this tumour umbrella.
Combined immunodeficiency; hearing loss 2/2, intellectual disability 2/4 and bronchiectasis 1/1 support additional axes, although reported samples are small.
Structural diverticulum of the urinary bladder; the urinary tract belongs to the renal axis.
Vertebral dysplasia with absent spinous processes, hemivertebrae, scoliosis and coxa vara; no spinal cord disease established.
Developmental overgrowth of an upper limb; no specific vascular, cutaneous or neurologic lesion is established.
Bacterial infection with a defining hemorrhagic disorder; additional organ injury is not established across the umbrella.
Copper transport disorder with neurodegeneration; pulmonary hypoplasia and cardiac enlargement/regurgitation each reported in 1/1; skeletal defects omitted by cap.
Viral infection defined by hemorrhagic manifestations; meningitis, pneumonia and nephrosis occur only in some cases without evidence of a 30% frequency.
Aortic aneurysm and skeletal connective-tissue abnormalities define disease; gingival overgrowth in 2/3 supports oral involvement; striae and proptosis lack established dysfunction.
Inherited abnormal platelet responsiveness, a blood-cell function defect.
Ichthyosis, intellectual deficit and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define disease; ocular abnormalities occur in 30-79%; skeletal involvement omitted by cap.
Progressive dystonia and parkinsonism; swallowing and voice dysfunction reflect neurologic motor impairment rather than separate gastrointestinal or airway damage.
Inherited lipoic acid biosynthesis defect; regression, abnormal myelination and cerebellar atrophy reported in 1/1; hepatic and cardiovascular injury frequencies unspecified.
